newsitem.title: USA: US rail carloads freight off from year ago-AAR.
newsitem.headline: US rail carloads freight off from year ago-AAR.

text.p: U.S. rail carload freight fell slightly in the week ended May 17 from the year-ago week due to declines in loadings of grain and coal, the Association of American Railroads said Thursday.

AAR said total carloads were 348,181 in the week, down 0.5 percent from 349,782 in the year-ago week. Loadings of grain were off 5.9 percent to 20,001 from 21,254 a year ago, while coal carloads fell two percent to 131,430 from 134,174.
But AAR said intermodal freight, which does not include carloads, continued strong, up 8.3 percent to 167,928 trailers and containers last week compared with 155,090 in the year-ago week.
AAR said ton-miles fell 0.4 percent to 26.3 billion from 26.4 billion a year ago. The ton-mile, a measure of freight transportation, is one ton of freight hauled one mile.

But despite the decline in total carloads, AAR said loadings of metals and related products increased 5.9 percent to 12,408 carloads in the May 17 week from 11,714 in the year-ago week. Farm products other than grain also rose 5.4 percent to 1,646 carloads from 1,562.
Chemicals loadings increased 5.4 percent to 31,618 carloads last week from 29,991 in the same 1996 week, while petroleum carloads totaled 5,828, up 3.9 percent from 5,607.
But AAR said nonmetallic minerals loadings fell 4.3 percent to 9,568 carloads last week from 10,000 a year ago. Motor vehicles and equipment also fell 3.9 percent to 21,707 carloads from 22,592.

In the first 20 weeks of 1997, AAR said carloads increased 1.8 percent to 6.77 million from 6.65 million in the same 1996 period. Trailers and containers rose 6.4 percent to 3.22 million from 3.03 million, while ton-miles increased 2.3 percent in the period to 530.7 billion from 518.8 billion.

AAR also said carloads on the two U.S. Canada-based railroads totaled 55,499 in the May 17 week, up 4.3 percent from a year ago, and 25,899 trailers and containers, up 11.8 percent from the same week last year.
For the first 20 weeks of 1997, the two railroads had 1.06 million carloads, up 0.9 percent from the year-ago period, and 486,051 trailers and containers, up 10.6 percent from last year, AAR said.

Combined total volume in the United States and Canada for the first 20 weeks was 7.82 million carloads, up 1.7 percent from the same 1996 period, while intermodal traffic totaled 3.71 million trailers and containers, up seven percent from last year, AAR said.
